KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions with heat indices 
around 105F are expected through the rest of the week. Heat 
Advisories remain in effect for nearly the entire area through 
this evening, and have been issued for central and SE portions 
of the area on Friday. 

The backdoor front has slowly lifted north and lingers near our 
northern CWA border this afternoon. Upper heights have slowly risen 
with a 594dm upper high centered from TN to the Carolinas. Isolated 
convection has developed to our north and west. Heat Advisories 
remain in effect for all areas except the MD/NC beaches. While 
temperatures have been a few degrees cooler than expected, dew pts 
in the mid to upper 70s have allowed mach of the area to reach Heat 
Advisory criteria (aside from the eastern shore). Regardless, will 
let the current advisories run until 8 PM. The ridge starts to break 
down and a cold front will approach from the north going into 
Friday, though temps in the mid to locally upper 90s and lower-mid 
70s dew pts along/east of I-95 will allow heat indices to peak in 
the 105-109F range across the SE 2/3 of the area. Therefore, have 
issued another round of Heat Advisories from 11 AM-8 PM from I-95 
east and roughly I-64 south.

Afternoon clouds and storms ahead of the front will likely limit 
temps across the north, and lower dew pts in the Piedmont may limit 
heat indices to the low 100s. So have held off on advisories attm 
for these area. Relief from the heat will come this weekend with no 
additional advisories anticipated. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...A few thunderstorms are possible mainly across 
northern portions of the area this evening and tonight (possibly 
severe with damaging winds). More widespread storms are expected on 
Friday, with storm chances continuing on Saturday (mainly SW). Some 
storms may be severe with damaging wind gusts and possibly large 
hail (especially on Friday).

As mentioned above, a few thunderstorms have developed to our NW 
this afternoon, but will struggle to reach the area through 4 PM as 
mesoanalysis shows some CIN/subsidence in place and the best 
forcing/upper flow is still across the southern Great Lakes and 
northern Mid-Atlantic. It remains uncertain whether the storms to 
our north will be able to make it into the Piedmont/central VA this 
evening, with PoPs generally no higher than 30% through 8 PM. 
However, if storms are able to make it down here, they could be 
strong to severe with damaging wind gusts. Another round of storms 
is possible overnight across our N and NE counties as a 
southwesterly 925-850mb jet strengthens some, with the most likely 
timing for this from 10 PM-3 AM (best storm chances overnight are 
across the MD Eastern Shore).

The most favorable overlap of forcing, shear, and instability is 
expected Friday. At the surface, the aforementioned front to our 
north will approach the local area but remain just to our north. 
Aloft, NW flow will remain in place and strengthen to 35-45 kt 
across much of the area by late in the day. The strong surface 
heating and humidity will allow for ample instability, and dry mid 
levels should enhance the potential for strong to severe winds. With 
falling upper heights and the approaching front, scattered to 
potentially numerous storms are expected to develop during the aftn 
and spread southeast through the evening. Given the overlap of 
strong heating/instability and deep-layer shear, continue to think 
that there is a legitimate severe wx threat for much of the area, 
with the potential for several fast-moving clusters capable of 
severe (50kt+) wind gusts, along with isolated marginal supercell 
structures capable of producing large hail (and damaging winds) as 
well. The lack of LLVL shear and high LCLs will greatly limit the 
tornado threat. The most likely timing for storms is between 4-10 PM 
with the highest storm coverage closer to the coast. SPC has 
maintained the Slight Risk (Level 2 out of 5) for severe wx across 
the entire area on Friday. 

The risk for storms (and any potential severe weather) Saturday is 
dependent on where the front is situated during peak heating. The 
12z/03 models have trended slightly slower with the front, and while 
winds switch to the north across the majority of the area Sat 
aftn...the main push of cooler/drier air may hold off until late 
Saturday. Therefore, it appears as if scattered storms are possible 
across a decent portion of the area along/south of I-64. There 
severe wx risk on Saturday is lower than on Friday, though a few 
storms could produce damaging wind gusts (especially across far 
southern portions of the area). Storms should be moving fast enough 
on Fri/Sat for no worse than a highly localized flood threat. 
Cooler/drier wx with onshore flow is expected on Sunday and Monday, 
with a gradual warm up after that (w/ mainly dry wx).
